name: Isaiah
charge: Answering the Lord’s call; prophesying judgment and redemption through persecution and rejection
summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up upon a throne, with seraphim crying Holy, holy, holy. His unclean lips were cleansed with a coal from the altar, and he answered, Here am I; send me. He walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia, counseled Hezekiah against Sennacherib, and prophesied the angel that smote 185,000 Assyrians in one night.
offense: In the year that King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. Above it stood the seraphims, each with six wings, crying one to another, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory. The posts of the door moved at the voice, and the house was filled with smoke (Isaiah 6:1–4). Isaiah cried, Woe is me, for I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips, for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts. A seraphim flew with a live coal from the altar and laid it upon his mouth, saying his iniquity was taken away and his sin purged (Isaiah 6:5–7). He heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? And he answered, Here am I; send me (Isaiah 6:8). He was sent to a people whose hearts were made fat, whose ears were heavy, whose eyes were shut, lest they see, hear, understand, convert, and be healed. The blindness was decreed until the cities be wasted and the land utterly desolate (Isaiah 6:9–11). At the Lord’s command, Isaiah walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia, that the king of Assyria would lead them away captive, young and old, naked and barefoot, to the shame of Egypt (Isaiah 20:2–4). The prophet’s body became the sign, and the sign endured for three years.
